claim_or_use: Computational propaganda became organized and global before generative AI
source: Bradshaw & Howard, The Global Disinformation Order (Oxford Internet Institute, 2019)
evidence_note: Documents organized social-media manipulation across 70 countries and the use of automation, algorithms and data in political communication.
caution: Inventory establishes deployment, not uniform effectiveness.

claim_or_use: Professionalization of organized social-media manipulation
source: Bradshaw, Bailey & Howard, Industrialized Disinformation (Oxford Internet Institute, 2020)
evidence_note: Documents organized manipulation in 81 countries and the growing role of private strategic-communications firms.
caution: Country presence does not measure persuasion or election effects.

claim_or_use: Computational propaganda is prior art rather than a new Deceptatron claim
source: Oxford Internet Institute Computational Propaganda project
evidence_note: Long-running research program on algorithms, automation and politics.
caution: Use as conceptual and empirical prior art.

claim_or_use: Personalized GPT-4 debate can outperform human debate in a controlled setting
source: Salvi et al., On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4, Nature Human Behaviour (2025)
evidence_note: Preregistered N=900 study; personalized GPT-4 increased odds of greater post-debate agreement by 81.2% relative to human-human baseline; among non-ties it was more persuasive 64.4% of the time.
caution: Not an 81.2% conversion rate; ten-minute debates and immediate agreement measures do not establish durable voting behavior.

claim_or_use: LLM-generated policy messages can shift attitudes
source: Bai et al., LLM-generated messages can persuade humans on policy issues, Nature Communications (2025)
evidence_note: Three preregistered experiments, total N=4,829; AI-generated persuasive messages produced attitude change relative to neutral controls and were broadly comparable with lay-human messages.
caution: Attitude movement in experiments is not equivalent to real-world behavior change.

claim_or_use: AI dialogue can affect candidate preferences across election contexts
source: Lin et al., Persuading voters using human–artificial intelligence dialogues, Nature (2025)
evidence_note: Preregistered experiments in the 2024 U.S., 2025 Canadian and 2025 Polish elections found significant treatment effects on candidate preference; reported effects exceeded typical traditional video-ad effects in the studied settings.
caution: Experimental exposure and measured candidate preference should not be generalized to population-scale election outcomes.

claim_or_use: Cheap conversational persuasion changes the economics even without mind control
source: Salvi et al., Nature Human Behaviour (2025)
evidence_note: Shows a general-purpose model can conduct personalized multiround persuasion at machine scale in a controlled setting.
caution: Scale is technically plausible; strategic impact in actual campaigns remains an empirical question.

claim_or_use: Generated persuasive text can be competitive with ordinary human text
source: Bai et al., Nature Communications (2025)
evidence_note: AI messages were similarly effective overall to lay-human persuasive messages across tested policy issues.
caution: Does not show superiority to professional campaign communication.

claim_or_use: Adaptive systems can choose among authentic material; truthfulness does not remove selection effects
source: C2PA Explainer
evidence_note: C2PA explicitly separates provenance from whether content is true, accurate or factual.
caution: Supports authenticity/truth distinction, not a causal claim about recommendation.

claim_or_use: Commercial systems can operationalize granular behavioral data without transferring a human-readable dossier
source: FTC Surveillance Pricing Study initial findings (2025)
evidence_note: FTC staff reported intermediaries could use location, browser history, shopping history, demographics and even mouse movements to tailor prices or promotions.
caution: Study concerns pricing, not political persuasion; use as evidence of operationalized behavioral personalization infrastructure.

claim_or_use: Targeting can come to the data rather than requiring a sponsor to receive raw personal data
source: FTC Surveillance Pricing Update & The Work Ahead (2025)
evidence_note: Describes broad first-, third-party and inferred data available to intermediaries for individualized commercial decisions.
caution: Analogy to political influence must be labeled as an analogy.

claim_or_use: The Deceptatron is a composition thesis, not a claim of one existing superweapon
source: Oxford Internet Institute Computational Propaganda project
evidence_note: Establishes that automation, algorithms and political manipulation were already studied as connected systems before generative AI.
caution: Novelty claim is the closed adaptive relationship synthesis, not the underlying components.

claim_or_use: Conversational persuasion is a demonstrated component of the proposed loop
source: Salvi et al., Nature Human Behaviour (2025)
evidence_note: Personalized multiround debate provides evidence for adaptive conversational persuasion as a component capability.
caution: Does not demonstrate an end-to-end covert propaganda stack.

claim_or_use: Political AI dialogue has measurable persuasive capacity
source: Lin et al., Nature (2025)
evidence_note: AI conversations shifted candidate preferences in multiple election contexts in experiments.
caution: Capability evidence only; not evidence that real operators have deployed a Deceptatron.

claim_or_use: Provenance authenticates claims about origin/history rather than truth
source: C2PA and Content Credentials Explainer v2.2
evidence_note: States that provenance can support origin/history/authenticity but alone cannot establish that content is true, accurate or factual.
caution: Do not frame this limitation as a failure of C2PA; it is an explicit non-goal.

claim_or_use: A valid provenance manifest can accompany misinformation
source: C2PA Harms Modelling v2.4
evidence_note: States that valid manifests do not make content true and that assets with valid manifests can still be misinformation or disinformation.
caution: Likewise, absence of Content Credentials does not imply content is untrustworthy.

claim_or_use: Unsigned media must not be treated as presumptively false
source: C2PA Harms Modelling v2.4
evidence_note: Explicitly warns that lack of Content Credentials does not mean content should not be trusted.
caution: Important for citizen journalism, legacy media and uneven adoption.

claim_or_use: Granular personal data can already influence individualized commercial treatment
source: FTC Surveillance Pricing Study initial findings (2025)
evidence_note: Evidence that location, browsing, shopping and interaction signals can be operationalized in individualized decision systems.
caution: Supports purpose-limitation argument by analogy; does not establish political use.

claim_or_use: Provenance should create inspectable friction without becoming a truth score
source: C2PA Harms Modelling v2.4
evidence_note: Separates validation of provenance information from truth judgments.
caution: Policy recommendations in manuscript are author's synthesis.

claim_or_use: Defensive attribution should distinguish operations from opinions
source: Oxford Internet Institute 2019 and 2020 inventories
evidence_note: Operational research focuses on organized manipulation actors, organizational forms and techniques rather than merely labeling disagreeable content.
caution: Specific democratic-counterintelligence doctrine is author's synthesis.

claim_or_use: AI persuasion should be treated as measurable but not omnipotent
source: Salvi et al.; Bai et al.; Lin et al. (2025)
evidence_note: Taken together, the studies support measurable machine persuasion and personalization/dialogue effects while leaving major external-validity questions open.
caution: Do not collapse distinct designs, outcomes or populations into one effect size.

claim_or_use: Authenticity infrastructure cannot substitute for shared judgment
source: C2PA Explainer and Harms Modelling
evidence_note: C2PA's explicit non-truth function supports the manuscript's closing distinction between establishing provenance and establishing political meaning.
caution: Normative conclusion belongs to the author, not C2PA.
